large_file_patching.rule: For files >500 lines (bot.py, engineer-chat/main.py, *.html, *.js, *.css), NEVER replace entire file. ALWAYS use patcher scripts with precise block replacement.
large_file_patching.why: Full replacement causes merge conflicts, token waste, risks partial writes. Block replacement via Python patcher is safer and faster.
large_file_patching.pattern: 1) Identify exact block to change via unique anchor lines. 2) Use Python patcher with .replace(old, new). 3) Apply via PowerShell: py patcher_NN.py; git add/commit/push.
large_file_patching.html_support: HTML/CSS/JS work the same вЂ” anchor to unique parent tags with id or data-attribute, unique classes, or distinctive text content. Example: replace '<section id="dashboard">...</section>' block. For CSS: target specific selector blocks like '.profile-card { ... }'. For JS: target specific function definitions like 'function renderProfile() { ... }'. Always use the most unique ancestor element to avoid false matches. Avoid regex across multiple lines вЂ” use exact multi-line string matching.
large_file_patching.powershell_three_block:
For large files (bot.py, engineer-chat, HTML), ALWAYS provide patcher as three PowerShell blocks:
BLOCK 1: New-Item -ItemType File -Path patcher_NN_name.py -Force  (creates empty file)
BLOCK 2: Full Python patcher code (copy-paste into the opened file and save)
BLOCK 3: py patcher_NN_name.py; Remove-Item patcher_NN_name.py; git add bot.py; git commit -m '...'; git pull --rebase origin main; git push

CRITICAL: Gardener only copies, pastes, presses Enter. Each block is ONE action.
Block 2 is the entire patcher script вЂ” ready to save and execute. Never split patcher code across multiple messages.

patcher_safety.no_cyrillic_in_string_literals: NEVER put Cyrillic or emoji directly inside patcher string literals. On Windows the file encoding mismatch (CP1251 vs UTF-8) corrupts the characters when the patcher writes bot.py. Use string concatenation instead: "text" + variable + "text".
patcher_safety.no_newlines_in_fstrings: NEVER use \n inside multiline f-string literals in patcher code. Python interprets them as real newlines, breaking string syntax on the target file. Use explicit string concatenation across lines.
patcher_safety.syntax_check_mandatory: ALWAYS add to BLOCK 3: python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('bot.py').read()); print('Syntax OK')" — commit ONLY after Syntax OK is confirmed. This prevents broken deploys.
patcher_safety.anchor_verification: ALWAYS add assert before replace: assert old in src, "Anchor not found". Never patch blindly — if anchor is missing the script must fail loudly, not silently skip.
patcher_safety.test_before_commit: Pattern: 1) apply patcher 2) run syntax check 3) only then git add/commit/push. Never skip step 2.
patcher_safety.anchor_by_content_not_line: NEVER use hardcoded line numbers to find insertion points. Line numbers shift after every insert/delete. ALWAYS search by unique string content: for i, line in enumerate(lines): if 'unique anchor text' in line: ...
patcher_safety.insert_outside_structures: When inserting code, verify the insertion point is OUTSIDE dict literals, function args, and other structures. Always print 3 lines before and after insertion to verify correct context.
patcher_safety.repr_before_patcher: ALWAYS read target lines via python3 -c "with open('bot.py', encoding='utf-8') as f: lines=f.readlines(); print(repr(lines[N]))" before building any patcher. Never construct anchors from sed output or visual inspection — encoding mismatches cause silent anchor failures.
patcher_safety.check_logs_after_restart: ALWAYS append log check to BLOCK 3 after systemctl restart. Pattern: ssh root@91.99.149.226 "cd /opt/mandala && git pull && systemctl restart mandala-bot && journalctl -u mandala-bot -n 50 --no-pager". Never report deploy success without seeing logs.
